subject: general
question: The radii of the circular ends of a frustum of a cone are 20 cm and 13 cm and its height is 12 cm. What is the capacity (in litres) of the frustum (correct to one decimal place)? (Take π = 22/7)
solution:
**Given:**

The radii of the circular ends of a frustum of a cone = 20 cm and 13 cm

Height = 12 cm

**Formula used:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b86141ce8528bbecfe394ac8e88d65be68cb8be8d220577b0fd3b63c094f09f0.png] 

Volume of frustum shaped cone = 1/3π(R² + r² +Rr)h

**Calculation:**

According to the question

Let R = 20 cm and r = 13 cm

Now,

Volume of frustum shaped cone = 1/3π(R2 + r2 +Rr)h

⇒ [1/3 × 22/7 × (20² + 13² + 20 × 13) × 12]

⇒ [1/3 × 22/7 × (400 + 169 + 260) × 12]

⇒ (1/3 × 22/7 × 829 × 12) cm³

⇒ (22/7 × 829 × 4) cm³

⇒ (72,952/7) cm³

⇒ 10,421.71 cm³

Now,

The capacity of frustum in litres = (10,421.71/1,000) litres

⇒ 10.4 litres

**∴ The capacity of frustum in litres is 10.4**
